title: Linear algebra II: vector spaces, inner products and spectral theory
audience: a college student in a mathematics degree program (or a related major such as physics, computer science or economics), or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Study linear algebra as mathematicians use it: abstract vector spaces, bases and dimension, linear maps and their matrices, quotients and duality, eigenvalues and invariant subspaces, inner product spaces and orthogonality, the spectral theorem, the singular value decomposition, determinants and traces, and the Jordan form, with proofs and with computation in Python.
primary_reading: Linear Algebra Done Right by Sheldon Axler, 4th edition (free, open access)

weeks.1: Vector spaces and subspaces over a field
weeks.2: Span, linear independence, bases and dimension
weeks.3: Linear maps, null spaces and ranges
weeks.4: Matrices of linear maps, change of basis, quotients and duality
weeks.7: Inner product spaces, norms and orthonormal bases
weeks.8: Gram–Schmidt, orthogonal projection and least squares
weeks.9: Self-adjoint and normal operators: the spectral theorem
weeks.10: Positive operators, isometries and the singular value decomposition
weeks.12: Generalized eigenvectors and the Jordan form

blocks.deliverable: Prove that a supplied set is a basis and find the dimension of a subspace.
Prove the rank–nullity theorem and apply it to a supplied map.
Decide which supplied operators are diagonalizable and prove it.
Week 7 midterm; prove a projection result and compute a least-squares fit.
Prove the spectral theorem for real symmetric 2 × 2 matrices and compute an SVD.
Find the Jordan form of a supplied matrix and justify each step.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Spectral portfolio: prove three structure theorems in full (rank–nullity, the spectral theorem for real symmetric matrices and the existence of the singular value decomposition), implement Gram–Schmidt, the power method and a small singular value decomposition in plain Python, and apply them to least squares, image compression or a Markov chain with a written explanation of every step.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
